observations: body L1, L3: «Al–Bat-» and «Chaldaeo–Graecos» have long dashes (5.2 and 5.1 pt); the hyphen at the end of L1 prints short (1.7 pt).
body L8, L22: both formulas are labelled «(α)» at the left margin; each formula is centred where it is printed.

body L8-L13: the formula is the rule of the right spherical triangle of L13 with the latitude of the Moon as the cathetus, the greatest latitude (the inclination of the orbit) as the angle opposite it and the argument of latitude as the hypotenuse: sin latit. : sin max. lat. = sin argum. : R. The declination of the Sun follows from the same rule with the obliquity for the inclination and the longitude for the argument.

body L9: the addenda (Part I, p. LXXIV) correct this statement: the rule is in Ptolemy, who says (V, 7; ed. Halma I, 315) that he computed the table of the latitude of the Moon «eadem demonstratione (δείξει)» as the arcs of the circles through the poles of the equator between the equator and the ecliptic, that is the declinations of the Sun.

body L15: the head prints «l,» with a comma; the dash after «a)» measures 9.4 pt, that of «23–24» 4.2 pt. The lines cited are p. 77, L23-L24: «Ratio parallaxis latitudinis ad parallaxim longitudinis est ut ratio sinus anguli ad eius cosinum».

body L16, L18, L21: «360–62» (4.9 pt), «al–Battānī» (5.1 and 4.9 pt) and «4–6» (4.9 pt) have long dashes. P. 81, L4-L6 multiplies the parallax in altitude by the sines of the angles of longitude and of latitude and divides by 60ᵖ, as in L19-L20 with R = 60ᵖ and the angle of longitude the complement of A.
body L19-L22: dividing the first equation by the second gives the rule of L22; the squares of the two parallaxes add up to the square of the parallax in altitude, as p. 77, L24-L25 says.
body L23-L25: the dash after «b)» measures 9.8 pt, that of «25–27» 5.0 pt. A heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition, which goes on to p. 252; it quotes p. 77, L25-L27.

body L26-L32: the figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the ecliptic AB and the horizon AH as the arcs of circles fitted to the ink (radius 318.6 and 363.3 pt; both curve), the arc from the zenith Z through L, produced beyond the ecliptic to L′, as its eight dashes and the short piece that runs into the ecliptic at L; the bold italic letters and the word «horizon» in italic stand where they are printed.

notes_left L2, L4-L6, notes_right L3: the hyphens at the ends of these lines print as short marks or dots (0.9 to 1.5 pt); those of «dix-huit», «demi-siècle», «Bas-Empire», «Bouché-Leclercq» and «121-22» measure 2.4 to 3.1 pt.
notes_right L6-L7: the head and the tail of the Dragon are printed with the signs ☊ and ☋; «l. l.» is loco laudato, p. 250, L22-L23.
